name: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority

findings.headline: Mayoral Investment Fund programmes reprioritised with net reduction of £0.443m over MTFP; shift from capital to revenue delivery reflects updated delivery forecasts.
findings.detail: Review of the MIF portfolio concluded additional revenue funding is required for programme delivery while several capital allocations are no longer required at previous levels. MIF Revenue Programme budget increased by £1.182m and Capital Programme reduced by £1.625m in 2026/27. Changes affect Skills Innovation Fund, Active Travel, Town Centres & High Streets and Cost of Living initiatives.
findings.matters: Significant mid-year reprioritisation of delivery approach suggests previous capital intensity assumptions were incorrect, indicating either market changes in how programmes can be delivered or delivery challenges with capital-heavy approaches.
findings.figures: Net reduction £0.443m over MTFP; 2026/27: revenue increase £1.225m, capital decrease £1.837m
findings.quote: The review has concluded that additional revenue funding is required to support programme delivery, whilst several capital allocations are no longer required at the levels previously assumed.

findings.headline: £650k investment approved for Bus Service Delivery Review, a critical programme to transfer bus services control to the Combined Authority from April 2027.
findings.detail: The investment will fund specialist staffing, legal and consultancy support to deliver the transition covering workforce, contractual, financial, legal, ICT and governance arrangements. Funding is available from in-year treasury management income forecast to exceed budget by £1m overall. This represents a new material commitment not included in the original 2026/27 budget.
findings.matters: Material new commitment emerging mid-budget cycle signals either incomplete original planning or changed government requirements. The bus transition is critical to devolution objectives but represents delivery risk requiring significant management resource and signalling programme complexity.
findings.figures: £650k investment required; treasury management income forecast £1m over budget
findings.quote: The Bus Delivery Review is a critical transition programme to prepare the York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority for assuming bus delivery responsibilities from April 2027. The programme covers workforce, contractual, financial, legal, ICT and governance arrangements. A one-off investment of £650k is required to provide resource the project and secure specialist staffing, legal and consultancy support, ensuring the transfer is delivered safely, compliantly and to the required timetable.

findings.headline: Mayoral Capacity Funding: £1.500m budgeting error corrected in June outturn; government confirms allocation of £1.322m (£0.178m below original estimate).
findings.detail: The June outturn report incorrectly reduced the expenditure budget by £1.500m rather than increasing income to reflect anticipated capacity funding. Government has subsequently confirmed the actual allocation at £1.322m, representing a shortfall from the original estimate. This capacity funding is ring-fenced for core capacity investment to support organisation growth and enhanced devolution responsibilities.
findings.matters: Budget correction indicates an internal control issue in how funding allocations were processed. The shortfall from estimated amount affects the Authority's ability to fund core capacity investment. Both matter for credit assessment and governance confidence.
findings.figures: £1.500m error in June budget; £1.322m confirmed allocation versus £1.500m estimate; £0.345m additional staffing overspend in core services
findings.quote: The Budget Outturn Report considered by Cabinet in June 2026 incorrectly reflected an anticipated allocation of £1.500m of additional Mayoral Capacity Funding. In presenting this funding, the expenditure budget was reduced by £1.500m rather than increasing income. Government has since confirmed the additional Mayoral Capacity Funding allocation to be £1.322m, (which is lower than the original estimate of £1.500m).

findings.headline: Brownfield Housing Programme forecast shows £24.159m underspend (17.99% of capital budget) reflecting delivery delays in major schemes.
findings.detail: The underspend is primarily due to claims being linked to start-on-site milestones rather than MHCLG funding timing, and to several major schemes experiencing viability, procurement and planning challenges. The Housing Team is undertaking detailed reforecasting with delivery partners and will bring any consequential budget changes to Cabinet in a separate report. Delivery risks have been escalated to Economy Directorate Management Team with a management action plan in place.
findings.matters: A material underspend in a major housing programme indicates delivery risk or programme overambition. This affects the council's capital deployment efficiency and the pace at which it can deliver housing outcomes — material to lenders and to other councils designing similar programmes.
findings.figures: £24.159m underspend on Brownfield Housing Programme; £25.475m budget against forecast expenditure of £1.317m
findings.quote: The forecast underspend of £24.159m on the Brownfield Housing Programme reflects the rephasing of expenditure into future financial years. This is primarily due to Brownfield Housing Fund claims being linked to start-on-site milestones rather than the timing of MHCLG funding receipts currently reflected in the budget. In addition, several major schemes are experiencing viability, procurement and planning challenges, resulting in delays to anticipated expenditure.

findings.headline: Town Centres programme rebalances £1.1m from capital delivery to revenue funding
findings.detail: Town Centres & High Streets capital funding is reduced by £1,144,385 and revenue funding increased by exactly £1,144,385, indicating a structural shift in programme delivery model.
findings.matters: Large reallocations between capital and revenue for a single programme are unusual and signal delivery model change (infrastructure to grants/revenue support) or timing adjustment; peers track how councils rebalance.
findings.figures: TCHS Capital Budget Change: -£1,144,385. TCHS Revenue Budget Change: +£1,144,385.
findings.quote: Capital Vibrant & Sustainable Place C-TCHS Town Centres & High Streets 366,932 1,733,938 461,630 2,562,500 1,571,438 1,768,515 3,706,885 -1,144,385

findings.headline: Business Innovation Fund revenue cut £979,000, capital increased £949,000
findings.detail: BIF revenue funding reduced by £978,963; BIF capital funding increased by £948,721. Net reduction across the portfolio is £30,242.
findings.matters: Shifts between revenue and capital for the same programme indicate timing or delivery model change; a net cut to growth investment programmes tracks economic outlook.
findings.figures: BIF Revenue Budget Change: -£978,963. BIF Capital Budget Change: +£948,721.
findings.quote: Revenue Inclusive Economic Growth BIF Business Innovation Fund 745,202 1,268,576 662,734 2,676,512 989,895 1,920,378 3,655,475 -978,963

findings.headline: Cost of Living Plan support funding withdrawn entirely
findings.detail: Cost of Living Plan revenue funding planned across 2026-27 and 2027-28 has been removed. The latest budget total was £260,000; the proposed budget is £0 across all periods.
findings.matters: Withdrawal of a cost-of-living support scheme mid-year is unusual when such programmes are typically committed; this signals either financial constraint or policy reversal.
findings.figures: Cost of living plan Latest Budget Total: £260,000. Proposed Budget Total: £0.

findings.headline: Active Travel funding reduced by £854,145 across revenue and maintenance
findings.detail: Active Travel revenue is reduced by £667,672 and Active Travel maintenance & activation by £186,473, totalling £854,145 across Active Travel programmes.
findings.matters: Active Travel is a growth/modal shift priority for many councils; a significant mid-year cut signals either delivery risk or competing budget pressure affecting this policy area.
findings.figures: Active Travel revenue Budget Change: -£667,672. Active Travel M&A Budget Change: -£186,473.

findings.headline: MIF programme budgets reduced by £612,635 for 2026-27 following Q1 review
findings.detail: The council's Medium-term Investment Framework review, dated 13 August 2026, has revised down the proposed MIF budget for 2026-27. The latest forecast was £16.94m; the proposed budget is now £16.33m. The net reduction is £612,635. For 2027-28, budgets increase by £169,585.
findings.matters: Material mid-year reductions to discretionary programme spending indicate either revised forecast conditions or budget pressure; peer finance directors track how councils adjust planned investment programmes in-year.
findings.quote: Budget Change -612,635 169,585

findings.headline: Active Travel capital programme forecast to deliver £264k against £1.6m budget.
findings.detail: The Capital Active Travel programme shows adjusted budget of £1,575k but forecast outturn of only £264k, a variance of £1,311k. Q1 actuals are £132k. This is the second-largest capital underspend after housing brownfield.
findings.matters: Active Travel investment is a council priority; material capital variances are relevant to assessing deployment capacity and the reliability of budget forecasting across the portfolio.
findings.figures: Latest budget £1,575k, forecast £264k, variance £1,311k, Q1 actuals £132k
findings.quote: Transport MIF - Capital C-AT Capital Active Travel 1,225 350 1,575 132 264 1,311

findings.headline: Combined Authority portfolio forecast to underspend by £22.2m (10% of full-year budget).
findings.detail: The Grand Total across all programmes shows latest budget of £217,297k with forecast outturn of £195,079k, a variance of £22,218k. Q1 actuals to date are £12,880k (5.9% of annual budget). The underspend is driven primarily by the housing capital variance above plus additional capital variances elsewhere in the portfolio.
findings.matters: Budget forecast accuracy is material to credit assessment and service planning; a 10% portfolio-wide variance indicates planned spending will not occur as allocated and reflects constraints in capital deployment.
findings.figures: Latest budget £217,297k, forecast £195,079k, variance £22,218k, Q1 actuals £12,880k

findings.headline: Housing Brownfield capital programme forecast to deliver £999k against £25.2m budget.
findings.detail: The Capital Brownfield programme shows adjusted budget of £25,158k but forecast outturn of only £999k, a variance of £24,159k. The original budget of £16,511k was increased by £8,647k at Q1 adjustments, but the forecast indicates the full amount will not be deployed. Q1 actuals to date are £28k.
findings.matters: Housing investment is a key council spending area; a £24m gap between budget and forecast indicates planned spending will not occur as budgeted and affects both service delivery outlook and credit assessment.
findings.figures: Latest budget £25,158k, forecast £999k, variance £24,159k, Q1 actuals £28k
findings.quote: Housing Capital Grant C-CB Capital Brownfield 16,511 8,647 25,158 28 999 24,159

findings.paper_title: YNYCA - Audit Strategy and Completion Report - 24-25 - signed
findings.headline: No fraud or non-compliance with laws and regulations identified during audit; management co-operation positive throughout
findings.detail: Auditors report finding no instances of fraud or material non-compliance with laws and regulations. However this is qualified: 'We have not undertaken any further work in these areas and do not provide any assurance.' Auditors note that 'management engaged positively throughout and we were able to work together to reach a way forward' and no significant audit difficulties were experienced despite complex issues requiring discussion.
findings.matters: Absence of identified fraud or compliance issues is positive. The qualifier is important—limited audit scope means absence of findings is not assurance. Constructive engagement from management despite audit challenges is noteworthy.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: We have no matters to report in relation to fraud and the Combined Authority's compliance with laws and regulations. We have not undertaken any further work in these areas and do not provide any assurance.

findings.paper_title: YNYCA - Audit Strategy and Completion Report - 24-25 - signed
findings.headline: No substantive testing performed on any account balances or transactions; audit scope fundamentally curtailed by backstop arrangement
findings.detail: Auditors state explicitly: 'Due to the backstop, we have not undertaken substantive testing procedures on any balances or transactions reported in the accounts.' Substantive testing is the primary audit procedure to verify account balances are correct and complete. Its absence means accounts have received no detailed verification work, compounding the impact of the disclaimed opinion.
findings.matters: Substantive testing is core audit work that provides evidence account balances are materially correct. Without it, and without an audit opinion, users of accounts have no independent verification that figures are accurate. This amplifies the impact of no audit assurance.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: Due to the backstop, we have not undertaken substantive testing procedures on any balances or transactions reported in the accounts.

findings.paper_title: YNYCA - Audit Strategy and Completion Report - 24-25 - signed
findings.headline: Material disclosure misstatements identified in accounts; government grants in Note 15 increased by £8.1m during audit
findings.detail: Auditors' initial review identified material disclosure misstatements which management corrected. Note 15 (Capital Financing and Capital Expenditure) was amended: government grants and other contributions increased from £40,034k to £48,113k, a change of £8,079k. Note 29 (Defined Benefit Pension Schemes) was restructured to separately show asset ceiling adjustment. No other material misstatements were identified. No assurance is provided on these corrections given the disclaimed opinion.
findings.matters: Material errors indicate quality control gaps in accounts preparation. The scale of the grant correction (£8m) is significant. Combined with documented capacity constraints, this suggests accounts are produced under pressure without adequate review cycles. Finance directors need confidence in accounts quality.
findings.figures: £48,113k (corrected) versus £40,034k (original); increase of £8,079k
findings.quote: Our initial review of the accounts noted a material disclosure misstatement which management have amended the financial statements for.

findings.paper_title: YNYCA - Audit Strategy and Completion Report - 24-25 - signed
findings.headline: Draft accounts published 13 August 2025, after 30 June statutory deadline; driven by finance team capacity constraints and reliance on key individuals
findings.detail: Accounts for 2024/25 were published on 13 August 2025, missing the 30 June statutory deadline by six weeks. This is the second consecutive year accounts have been published late. Auditors found the combined authority 'overly reliant on key officers, specifically the Section 73 Officer, and third-party arrangements when managing the General Budgets.' Staff departures have occurred and pressure on senior officers continues. Additional accountants are planned to start late 2025 and early 2026, but have not yet commenced.
findings.matters: Publication delays miss statutory deadlines and signal the finance function cannot keep pace with workload. Key person reliance creates risk if the S73 Officer departs or is unavailable. Lenders assess whether finance teams have capacity to manage their responsibilities reliably.
findings.figures: Accounts published 13 August 2025 (44 days late); prior year published 16 January 2025 (missing 31 May 2024 deadline); recruitment starts late 2025
findings.quote: However, despite this, in 2024-25 the Combined Authority appeared to be overly reliant on key officers, specifically the Section 73 Officer, and third-party arrangements when managing the General Budgets.

findings.paper_title: YNYCA - Audit Strategy and Completion Report - 24-25 - signed
findings.headline: Medium-Term Financial Strategy absent for combined authority's general budget; not expected until 2026/27 budget cycle
findings.detail: No MTFS is in place for the combined authority's general budget for 2024/25 onwards. Auditors recorded management's indication in February 2025 that it would be ready in 'late 2025'; it is now expected as part of 2026/27 budget development. Quarterly budget monitoring has been implemented and high-level medium-term view is reported in 2025/26 budget, but formal strategy remains absent. Police and Fire services have developed robust MTFSs.
findings.matters: An MTFS enables authorities to align resource allocation with strategy and identify funding gaps. Its absence creates risk of unidentified savings needs emerging mid-year. Finance directors at peer councils expect this as standard practice; its absence signals planning weakness.
findings.figures: No MTFS for 2024/25 or 2025/26; expected 2026/27
findings.quote: However, as of February 2025, there is no MTFS in place for the Combined Authority's general budget for 2024/25 or onwards.

findings.paper_title: YNYCA - Audit Strategy and Completion Report - 24-25 - signed
findings.headline: Four significant weaknesses in governance arrangements: one new in internal audit oversight, three continuing from prior year
findings.detail: One new weakness identified: Audit and Governance Committee did not receive internal audit updates from Police and Fire functions during 2024/25, limiting oversight of the combined authority's full internal control environment. Three weaknesses persist from 2023/24: absence of a Medium-Term Financial Strategy for general budget (expected 2026/27); risk and performance management arrangements not in place during 2024/25 (implemented from April 2025 onwards); finance team capacity issues with accounts published after statutory deadline despite planned recruitment.
findings.matters: Significant weaknesses mean the authority cannot demonstrate proper arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness. These persist or emerge despite audit recommendations. Each creates specific risks: missing MTFS means unidentified funding gaps; governance gaps mean inadequate oversight; capacity gaps mean delivery risk and key person dependence.
findings.figures: Four significant weaknesses identified; three continuing from prior year
findings.quote: During 2024/25 the Audit and Governance Committee did not receive regular update reports from the Internal Audit function of the Policing and Fire & Rescue functions.

findings.paper_title: YNYCA - Audit Strategy and Completion Report - 24-25 - signed
findings.headline: Second consecutive disclaimed opinion on financial statements; insufficient time to rebuild assurance before 27 February 2026 backstop date
findings.detail: Auditors issued a disclaimed opinion on 2023/24 accounts on 27 February 2025. For 2024/25, despite one intervening year, they conclude there is insufficient time to complete audit procedures to rebuild assurance before the statutory backstop date of 27 February 2026. They will again issue a disclaimed opinion, meaning two consecutive years with no audit assurance on accounts and opening balances.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means no assurance on account balances. Finance directors cannot rely on accounts for decisions; lenders cannot assess financial position. Two consecutive disclaimers signal that financial reporting or audit capability issues will require years to resolve, not months.
findings.figures: Backstop date 27 February 2026; previous disclaimer issued 27 February 2025
findings.quote: It has not been possible to complete sufficient procedures as part of the current year's audit to enable us to issue a non-disclaimed opinion.

findings.headline: General Budget borrowing utilisation rises from 50% to 57% of Debt Cap between 2025/26 and 2027/28, indicating tightening headroom.
findings.detail: General Budget Actual External Debt of £11.750m represents 54% of the Debt Cap (£21.750m) in 2026/27, up from 50% in 2025/26. The ratio continues to rise to 56.5% by 2027/28. While the council remains within its statutory limits, the declining headroom relative to planned capital spending warrants monitoring.
findings.matters: The rising proportion of available borrowing capacity being utilised, combined with growing capital financing requirements and reserve depletion, indicates less flexibility for unexpected funding needs.
findings.figures: Actual External Debt £11.750m (2026/27) against Debt Cap £21.750m (54% utilisation)
findings.quote: Actual External Debt Borrowing 9.900 11.750 13.000 13.000; Debt Cap 19.900 21.750 23.000 23.000

findings.headline: Police and Fire Rescue interest payable grows 80% over the forecast period, from £0.731m to £1.313m annually.
findings.detail: Interest payable on borrowing for Police Fire & Rescue rises from £0.731m in 2025/26 to £0.746m in 2026/27, then accelerates through £0.929m (2027/28) to £1.313m (2028/29). This growth reflects both existing debt service costs and the impact of new borrowing to fund the rising Capital Financing Requirement.
findings.matters: Rapidly escalating interest costs reduce the resources available for service delivery. The 80% increase over four years indicates significant exposure to the combined effects of existing and planned borrowing.
findings.quote: Interest payable on borrowing: Police Fire & Rescue 0.731 0.746 0.929 1.313

findings.headline: Interest receivable declines sharply for Police and Fire Rescue, falling 61% from £0.437m to £0.171m between 2025/26 and 2026/27.
findings.detail: Police Fire & Rescue interest receivable falls from £0.437m in 2025/26 to £0.171m in 2026/27 and remains at that level through 2028/29. Economic Directorate interest receivable also declines from £0.829m to £0.550m over the same period. These substantial reductions may indicate either smaller cash holdings available for investment or returns compressed by the interest rate environment.
findings.matters: Declining investment income may reflect either reduced liquidity or lower returns in the current rate environment. Combined with planned reserve drawdowns, it suggests cash positions are tightening.
findings.figures: Police & Fire: £0.437m → £0.171m; Economic: £0.829m → £0.550m
findings.quote: Interest receivable: Police Fire & Rescue -0.437 -0.171 -0.171 -0.171; Economic Directorate -0.829 -0.645 -0.550 -0.550

findings.headline: General Budget reserves projected to fall 73% from £25.5m to £7m by 2027/28, sharply reducing financial flexibility.
findings.detail: Under the Liability Benchmark framework, Resources on Balance Sheet for the General Budget decline from £25.500m in 2025/26 to £21.752m in 2026/27 and then drop sharply to £7.000m in 2027/28, where they remain through 2028/29. This planned drawdown of £18.5m in reserves indicates the council will rely increasingly on external debt financing.
findings.matters: Large planned reductions in reserve balances limit financial buffer and flexibility. The council's dependence on external borrowing increases as reserves are depleted, which affects both sustainability and lender risk assessment.
findings.quote: Resources on Balance Sheet: -25.500 -21.752 -7.000 -7.000

findings.headline: Capital Financing Requirement for Police and Fire Rescue grows 44% over four years, from £20.4m to £29.3m.
findings.detail: The opening Capital Financing Requirement for Police Fire & Rescue is £20.440m in 2025/26 and grows to £22.932m (2026/27), £23.598m (2027/28), and £27.254m (2028/29), closing at £29.340m. This sustained growth trajectory indicates significant capital commitments ahead and future borrowing needs.
findings.matters: Growing CFR signals future capital investment plans and the borrowing required to fund them. Lenders monitor this metric to assess the council's medium-term financial trajectory and sustainability.
findings.quote: Capital Financing Requirement opening 20.440 22.932 23.598 27.254; closing 22.932 23.598 27.254 29.340

findings.headline: Police and Fire Rescue finance costs rise to 5.8% of net revenue stream in 2026-27, up from 4.7% in 2025-26.
findings.detail: The ratio of finance costs to net revenue stream for Police Fire & Rescue increases from 4.7% in 2025/26 to 5.8% in 2026/27. This ratio moderates to 4.3% in 2027/28 before rising again to 5.0% in 2028/29. The increase indicates a growing proportion of the revenue budget is consumed by debt servicing costs.
findings.matters: Rising finance costs as a share of revenue constrains the council's spending flexibility and indicates mounting financial pressure from its borrowing programme.
findings.quote: Ratio of Finance Costs to net revenue stream: 4.7% 5.8% 4.3% 5.0%

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Combined Authority does not produce fully consolidated budget outturn reports to committees despite integrating three major services
findings.detail: Budget outturn reported separately for general, police and fire budgets to respective committees. Per Constitution, consolidated reporting not required. Authority produces group financial statements but does not consistently present consolidated outturn to committees or Mayor.
findings.matters: Structural reporting gap in newly integrated authority means committees and Mayor cannot see full financial picture; material governance weakness for finance directors at peer authorities.
findings.quote: Although the Combined Authority issues quarterly budget outturn reports for the general, police, and fire budgets and prepares Group Financial Statements, it does not consistently present a fully consolidated outturn budget reports to Committees or the Mayor.

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: North Yorkshire Police and Fire and Rescue both improved external inspection ratings
findings.detail: NYP PEEL inspection (March 2024) rated service Good or Adequate across all 10 themes — improvement from prior inspection. Fire and Rescue inspection (Dec 2024-Jan 2025) rated Good or Adequate across all 11 areas with no Requiring Improvement ratings — improvement from 2022 when rated Inadequate in efficiency and people.
findings.matters: External validation of improved operational performance in police and fire services despite governance framework gaps; positive indicator of service quality for finance directors and lenders.
findings.figures: March 2024, December 2024, January 2025
findings.quote: NYP were rates Good or Adequate across all of the 10 themes inspected. This is an improvement from the last inspection and shows them to be continually improving... the service were graded 'Good' or 'Adequate' in all 11 areas, with no areas assessed as 'Requiring Improvement'. This is an improvement from the last inspection in 2022

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Police service delivered £2,102k surplus before reserves and capital, underspend of £312k
findings.detail: Revised revenue budget £225,807k. Received £227,929k resulting in underspend £2,123k before reserves and capital. Delivered overall surplus £2,102k before reserves and capital, representing total underspend of £312k.
findings.matters: Large service operating effectively and delivering surplus, demonstrating operational control despite governance framework issues.
findings.quote: Received £227,929k in revenue resulting in an underspend of £2,123k. Overall delivered a surplus of £2,102k before reserves and capital, giving an overall underspend of £312k.

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: General Budgets delivered net surplus of £11,937k with underspend of £2.4m against budget
findings.detail: Core general budgets element performed well, underspending by £2.4m. Driven by increased treasury management income, lower staff costs and other non-staffing cost savings. Shows effective budget control in the core funding area.
findings.matters: Demonstrates that despite governance and capacity issues, core general budgets are well-controlled and delivering surplus; positive indicator within otherwise weak governance picture.
findings.quote: Net surplus of £11,937k giving a net underspend compared to budget of £2.4m. This was primarily driven by increased treasury management income, lower staff costs and other non-staffing cost savings.

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Audit and Governance Committee does not receive internal audit reports from Police and Fire functions; new significant weakness identified
findings.detail: Audit and Governance Committee receives internal audit reports only from Veritau (General Budgets). RSM internal audit reports for Police and Fire are reported separately to Joint Independent Audit Committee and Independent Audit Committee respectively. A&G therefore lacks visibility of full Combined Authority internal control environment and cannot properly discharge its governance role.
findings.matters: Structural governance gap means primary audit committee lacks oversight of two-thirds of the Combined Authority; material audit weakness for finance directors and lenders assessing governance structure.
findings.quote: Our review of A&G minutes confirms that RSM's internal audit findings for Police and Fire & Rescue are not routinely presented to A&G. Consequently, A&G does not have oversight of the entire Combined Authority's Internal Audit function and findings

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Overall performance management framework not yet formalised as of February 2025
findings.detail: While Combined Authority developed piecemeal performance arrangements (programme office, Adult Skills Fund framework, Local Evaluation Framework, interim corporate plan), no single overall performance management framework document with clearly defined KPIs linked to strategic objectives. Auditor previously recommended such a framework; authority has recruited performance manager to deliver it in 2025/26.
findings.matters: Cannot assess whether authority delivering value for money across all functions; material to lenders and finance directors evaluating whether authority can demonstrate effective performance.
findings.figures: February 2025
findings.quote: as of February 2025, the Combined Authority is currently still formalising their overall performance management framework document. The Authority also has plans to develop a single service delivery plan

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Risk Management Policy and Framework not finalised until April 2025; adequate arrangements not in place for most of 2024/25
findings.detail: Auditor found for most of 2024/25 adequate risk management arrangements were not in place. Authority subsequently developed Risk Management Policy, Framework, strategic and operational risk registers and started quarterly reporting to Audit and Governance Committee — all finalised April 2025 after year-end. Weakness originally identified in 2023/24.
findings.matters: Material gap in core governance function in newly integrated authority managing three major services (general budgets, police, fire); finance directors at peer authorities would assess this as material governance risk.
findings.quote: for most of 2024-25, adequate risk management arrangements were not in place. Progress has however been made in 2024/25 to develop key risk management documents which were finalised in April 2025

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Finance team over-reliant on key individuals with ongoing resourcing pressures, staff turnover and delayed VFM responses
findings.detail: Auditor found in 2024/25 over-reliance on Section 73 Officer and external support from North Yorkshire Council. Management discussions highlight ongoing resourcing pressures including staff turnover and increased demands on senior finance officers. Delays noted in responding to VFM requests and accounts were not published by national deadline.
findings.matters: Structural finance team weakness creates operational risk that critical financial controls and reporting cannot be reliably delivered; material to lenders and peer finance directors assessing governance capacity.
findings.quote: in 2024-25, there was a risk of over-reliance on key individuals— most notably the Section 73 Officer— as well as on external support arrangements with North Yorkshire Council in the management of the General Budgets. Discussions with management during the audit planning phase have further highlighted ongoing resourcing pressures, including staff turnover and increased demands on senior finance officers

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Fire and Rescue delivered deficit of £827k in 2024/25; Mayor increased fire precept by £24 Band D for 2025/26 (up from £2.41 prior year)
findings.detail: Fire service net deficit of £339k before reserve transfers; £827k including transfers, representing £488k overspend largely due to in-year pay awards. To address underinvestment and ensure long-term financial stability, Mayor increased fire precept by £24 for Band D properties in 2025/26 — compared to £2.41 movement in prior year.
findings.matters: Precept increases of this magnitude signal material service cost pressures that required intervention to stabilise the service; material to finance directors managing similar services and to those assessing authority financial trajectory.
findings.quote: Net deficit of £339k before reserve transfers... The Mayor increased the Fire precept for 2025/26 by £24 for Band D properties from 2024/25. This is a significant increase in comparison to the movement of £2.41 from 2023/24 to 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: No Medium-Term Financial Strategy in place as of February 2026, weakness first identified in 2023/24
findings.detail: Despite police and fire developing robust MTFSs for 2024/25 onwards, the Combined Authority has no MTFS covering 2024/25 onwards. Authority cites capacity constraints in finance team. Auditor has recommended producing and regularly updating an MTFS to support financial sustainability and align with strategic objectives.
findings.matters: Absence of MTFS prevents medium-term financial planning and makes it impossible to assess whether authority can sustain services; material governance weakness for any council assessing peer vulnerability.
findings.figures: February 2026, 2024/25
findings.quote: as of February 2026, there is no Medium-Term Financial Plan (MTFS) which covered 2024/25 onwards. A MTFS would include financial projections, analysis and context to support the delivery for the Combined Authority's key priorities

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Group financial statements published 13 August 2025, over six weeks after 30 June statutory deadline
findings.detail: The auditor attributes the delay to complexities in integrating data from three legacy financial systems and challenges consolidating the group accounts following the May 2024 transfer of Police and Fire functions. The authority has since recruited additional finance staff including a permanent Head of Finance from 2025/26.
findings.matters: Missing statutory deadlines signals capacity or control issues in finance function; matters to lenders and peer finance directors assessing governance maturity of a newly formed authority.
findings.figures: 13th August 2025, 30 June 2025
findings.quote: The Combined Authority's Group financial statements were published on 13th August 2025, after the statutory deadline of 30 June 2025. Management discussions indicate that this was largely driven by the complexities involved in the initial year of integrating data from three legacy financial systems

findings.paper_title: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority - Auditor's Annual Report 24-25 - FINAL (ID 19696844)
findings.headline: Auditor issued disclaimer of opinion on financial statements with no assurance provided
findings.detail: The auditor determined insufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained before the statutory deadline for publication. The audit report, issued 27 February 2026, modified to disclaimer rather than an opinion on whether statements present a true and fair view. This reflects timing pressure from the regulatory deadline.
findings.matters: A disclaimer of opinion provides no assurance to users that financial statements are correct — material to lenders and finance directors assessing creditworthiness and financial reliability.
findings.figures: 27 February 2026
findings.quote: We concluded we had not obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence to enable us to express an opinion on whether the financial statements present a true and fair view

findings.paper_title: 15042026_A&G_TMS Report - Appendix One - General Budget TMS 2026-27
findings.headline: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority General Budget holds no external debt and no planned borrowing for capital expenditure
findings.detail: The authority operates its General Budget entirely from in-year grants through delivery partners. All cash is held for treasury purposes only with no commercial return investments. All funds must remain fully liquid on 7-day notice.
findings.matters: A lender assessing credit risk would note the absence of debt and strong liquidity position; peer finance directors would observe how this authority manages a cash-generative operation without borrowing
findings.figures: General Budget external debt: nil; capital expenditure: only minor office equipment funded from in-year grants; non-specified investment limit: 20% of portfolio; investments over 365 days: nil
findings.quote: Currently, YNYCA's General Budget does not show a borrowing requirement for future capital expenditure and there is no existing external debt in relation to these budgets.

findings.paper_title: 15042026_A&G_TMS Report - Appendix One - General Budget TMS 2026-27
findings.headline: Investment performance benchmark changed from 7-day LIBID to SONIA following Bank of England discontinuation of LIBID
findings.detail: The authority's treasury framework now uses SONIA (Sterling Overnight Index Average) as the benchmark for internal investment portfolio performance, measured as a backward-looking 7-day compound rate over a quarter. This change was mandated by the discontinuation of LIBID publication.
findings.matters: LIBID discontinuation is a sector-wide issue affecting all authorities' treasury frameworks; SONIA is becoming the standard benchmark for measuring treasury investment performance across local government
findings.figures: Benchmark now: SONIA 7-day backward-looking compound rate measured quarterly (replacing 7-day LIBID)
findings.quote: It is important to understand that the benchmark has changed from previous years as the 7-day LIBID rate is no longer published by the Bank of England.

findings.paper_title: 15042026_A&G_TMS Report - Appendix One - General Budget TMS 2026-27
findings.headline: MUFG forecasts Bank Rate reductions to 3.5% in Q2 2026 and 3.25% in Q4, but flags increased uncertainty from geopolitical tensions
findings.detail: MUFG Corporate Markets revised its forecast on 22 December 2025 expecting Bank Rate cuts during 2026 following anticipated CPI falls. However, the document explicitly notes that recent geopolitical developments, including escalating Iran tensions, have heightened inflation risks and may delay or prevent the expected rate cuts.
findings.matters: Forward interest rate expectations directly affect borrowing costs and investment returns; any authority planning capital projects or managing cash positions needs these forecasts to assess refinancing costs and liquidity returns
findings.figures: Current Bank Rate 3.75% (reduced from 4.0%); forecast: 3.5% Q2 2026, 3.25% Q4 2026; current PWLB rates (22 December 2025): 5-year 4.81%, 10-year 5.39%, 25-year 6.01%, 50-year 5.78%
findings.quote: the MUFG Corporate Markets forecast has been revised to price in a rate cut in Q2 2026 to 3.5%, likely to take place in the wake of a significant fall in the CPI inflation reading from 3% in March to 2% in April (as forecast by Capital Economics), followed by a short lull through the summer whilst more data is garnered, and then a further rate cut to 3.25% in Q4

findings.headline: Group net reserves deficit of £1,467,060k driven by unfunded pension liabilities of Chief Constable and Fire Service
findings.detail: The group accounts show total negative net reserves of £1,467,060k versus single entity deficit of £177,861k. The increase is driven by consolidation of the Chief Constable's unfunded pension liability (£1,578,290k in group compared to £291,950k in single entity) and Fire and Rescue Service unfunded pension liabilities.
findings.matters: Unfunded pension liabilities represent a significant long-term financial obligation affecting the authority's balance sheet strength and financial capacity.
findings.figures: Group net reserves: (£1,467,060)k; Single entity net reserves: (£177,861)k; Group pension liabilities: (£1,578,290)k; Single entity pension liabilities: (£291,950)k
findings.quote: The overall negative net reserve position reflects the impact of unfunded pension liabilities of the Chief Constable (consolidated only) and Fire and Rescue Service (single entity)

findings.headline: Internal audit scope limited by first-year nature of newly integrated systems and controls
findings.detail: Internal audit scope has been constrained by the first-year integration of systems and controls following transfer of police and fire functions, reducing the level of audit assurance available.
findings.matters: Reduced audit scope means not all controls have been fully verified, affecting the overall governance and control assurance position during a period of significant organisational change.
findings.figures: Not stated
findings.quote: Scope limitations in internal audit due to the first-year nature of systems and controls.

findings.headline: Information governance weaknesses identified including FOI compliance below benchmark
findings.detail: Information governance weaknesses have been identified as a key issue and risk, including Freedom of Information response compliance that falls below benchmark levels and policy gaps.
findings.matters: Information governance and FOI compliance are indicators of transparency and public accountability in local authorities.
findings.figures: FOI compliance below benchmark level (specific benchmark not detailed)
findings.quote: Information governance weaknesses, including FOI compliance below benchmark and policy gaps.

findings.headline: Draft accounts publication delayed due to complexity of integrating multiple financial systems
findings.detail: Publication of draft accounts was delayed as a direct result of integrating multiple financial systems following the May 2024 transfer of fire and police functions. Delays resulted from first-year consolidation complexity.
findings.matters: Delayed accounts publication signals potential control or systems weaknesses and affects timeliness of financial reporting to stakeholders.
findings.figures: Not stated
findings.quote: Delayed publication of draft accounts due to the complexity of integrating multiple financial systems and functions.

findings.headline: No Medium-Term Financial Strategy was in place during 2024/25; development now underway
findings.detail: The authority did not have a multi-year financial strategy during the financial year, which is explicitly identified as a key issue. The MTFS is now under development.
findings.matters: A MTFS is fundamental for demonstrating financial sustainability and planning. Its absence during a year of major organisational integration represents a governance gap.
findings.figures: Not stated
findings.quote: Absence of a Medium-Term Financial Strategy (MTFS) during the year, now under development.

findings.headline: External auditor will issue disclaimed audit opinion under statutory backstop arrangement by 28 February
findings.detail: The auditor will not provide a full audit opinion but will issue a disclaimed audit opinion under the national audit backstop arrangement. This reflects the statutory deadline requirement rather than completion of a full audit.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion indicates the auditor cannot provide full independent verification of the financial statements, reducing assurance over the authority's reported financial position.
findings.figures: Statutory reporting deadline: 28 February 2026
findings.quote: In line with national audit backstop arrangements, the external auditor must issue a disclaimed audit opinion based on an approved set of accounts.

findings.headline: Fire and Rescue Service rated 'good' in six areas following HMICFRS inspection, down from 'inadequate' in two areas in 2021/22; improvement areas reduced from 24 to seven
findings.detail: HMICFRS inspected the Fire and Rescue Service during late 2024 and early 2025. The Service achieved six areas rated 'good' and five areas rated 'adequate' with no causes for concern identified. This represents significant progress from the previous 2021/22 inspection when the FRS had been rated 'inadequate' in two areas. Improvement areas required were reduced from 24 to seven.
findings.matters: HMICFRS ratings reflect service quality and compliance with national standards; this significant improvement demonstrates recovery from prior inadequacy ratings and suggests effective management intervention, reducing operational and reputational risk.
findings.figures: Six areas rated good, five adequate (2024/25); previously inadequate in two areas (2021/22); improvement areas: 7 (down from 24)
findings.quote: Key improvements included significant progress since the last inspection in 2021/2022, where the FRS had been rated "inadequate" in two areas, they now have six areas where they are rated "good" and five areas where they are rated "adequate", with no causes for concern identified. Improvement areas were reduced from 24 to seven.

findings.headline: Internal audit opinion for 2024/25 issued with scope limitations; four of six Fire audits achieved positive assurance but data quality and health and safety resulted in partial assurance
findings.detail: Veritau indicated that its year-end opinion for 2024/25 will reflect scope limitations due to the first operational year nature of systems and inability to obtain breadth of coverage typically required for full audit opinion. Fire Service internal audits showed four of six reviews achieving positive assurance while two (Data Quality and Health and Safety) resulted in partial assurance; Financial Planning was graded Substantial Assurance. Police internal audit identified some weaknesses that could lead to inadequacy if not addressed.
findings.matters: Scope limitations restrict the assurance available to assess control environment completeness; partial assurances in specific audit areas indicate control weaknesses requiring management action and ongoing monitoring.
findings.figures: Four of six Fire audits positive; 2 partial assurance; Financial Planning: Substantial Assurance
findings.quote: Veritau has indicated that its year-end opinion for 2024/25 will be issued with scope limitations. This reflects both the volume of new and developing systems in place during the Authority's first operational year, and the practical constraint that it was not possible to obtain the breadth of coverage typically required to support a full audit assurance opinion.

findings.headline: Freedom of Information compliance at 74%, below 90% benchmark; 29 information security incidents recorded during year
findings.detail: Routine oversight activity identified FOI compliance rate of 74%, below the 90% benchmark, and the Authority recorded 29 information security incidents during 2024/25, mostly from misdirected correspondence or procedural lapses. Information governance framework remains at early stage of development with core policies either absent, out of date, or inconsistently applied.
findings.matters: FOI compliance failures and information security incidents indicate governance and control weaknesses; this matters for transparency obligations and data protection compliance, both relevant to lender confidence in governance maturity.
findings.figures: 74% FOI compliance rate (90% benchmark); 29 information security incidents
findings.quote: The Authority recorded 29 information security incidents during the year, most resulting from misdirected correspondence or procedural lapses. The Freedom of Information (FOI) compliance rate stood at 74%, below the 90% benchmark.

findings.headline: Mayor approved £24 precept rise to stabilise Fire and Rescue Service reserves following public consultation
findings.detail: A key intervention by the Mayor was to opt for a £24 precept rise to stabilise reserves and enable essential investment in the Fire Service following a public consultation and significant concerns that the Fire and Rescue service's financial position could adversely impact performance and public safety.
findings.matters: Precept rises reflect how a mayoral authority responds to service funding pressures; this decision demonstrates active management of financial stress in a critical service and shows the Mayor's assessment that reserves required rebuilding.
findings.figures: £24 precept rise
findings.quote: A key intervention by the Mayor was to opt for a £24 precept rise to stabilise reserves and enable essential investment in the Fire and Service following a public consultation and significant concerns that the financial position of the Fire and Rescue service could adversely impact performance and ultimately public safety

findings.headline: Absence of Medium-Term Financial Strategy during 2023/24 reporting period; initial medium-term view approved February 2025
findings.detail: External auditors identified that the Authority did not have an MTFS in place during the reporting period, creating uncertainty in long-term resource allocation, investment decisions, and fiscal sustainability. An initial medium-term view was subsequently approved alongside the February 2025 budget, with a full MTFS now under development following the Summer 2025 Spending Review announcement.
findings.matters: Absence of an MTFS prevents assessment of whether the Authority has a sustainable financial plan and ability to manage medium-term funding pressures, a critical concern for lenders evaluating long-term viability.
findings.figures: February 2025 budget approval; Summer 2025 Spending Review
findings.quote: The auditors noted that the Authority did not have a Medium-Term Financial Strategy (MTFS) in place during the reporting period. They commented that without an MTFS, there was no structured approach to financial planning, creating uncertainty in long-term resource allocation, investment decisions, and fiscal sustainability.

findings.headline: 2024/25 draft Statement of Accounts not published by statutory 30 June deadline; statutory notice issued
findings.detail: Despite a detailed closedown action plan being prepared, the 2024/25 draft Statement of Accounts was not published by the statutory 30 June deadline. The delay was primarily due to complexity in consolidating data from three legacy financial systems (General Fund, Policing, Fire) during the first year of operation. A statutory notice was issued and work is ongoing to complete statements and assurance checks.
findings.matters: Failure to meet statutory publication deadlines for financial statements is a compliance failure and signals control weaknesses in financial processes that lenders assess when evaluating creditworthiness and governance risk.
findings.figures: Statutory 30 June deadline
findings.quote: Despite the detailed closedown action plan being prepared, the 2024/25 draft Statement of Accounts was not published by the statutory 30 June deadline. This was primarily due to the complexity of the first year of consolidating data from three legacy financial systems (General Fund, Policing, Fire)

findings.headline: 2023/24 audit received disclaimer of opinion due to insufficient audit evidence and resourcing constraints
findings.detail: Forvis Mazars issued a disclaimer of opinion on the financial statements for the two months to March 2025 as resourcing constraints both within the Combined Authority and the auditors led to insufficient audit evidence being gathered before the statutory publication deadline. This meant the audit could not be completed and no audit opinion was provided.
findings.matters: A disclaimer of opinion means lenders and other stakeholders cannot rely on independently audited financial information, creating uncertainty about the reliability of the Authority's financial position and controls.
findings.figures: 2023/24 reporting period
findings.quote: The External Auditors, Forvis Mazars, issued a disclaimer of opinion on the financial statements for the two months to March 2025 as resourcing constraints both within the CA and Auditors led to insufficient audit evidence being gathered before the statutory publication deadline.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Head of Internal Audit YNYCA report 2025
findings.headline: For most of 2024/25, adequate risk management arrangements were not in place; Audit and Governance Committee unable to fulfil oversight role
findings.detail: The authority lacked effective risk management arrangements for the majority of the year, preventing the Audit and Governance Committee from obtaining assurance on the effectiveness of the risk management framework. Work to establish risk management arrangements began during the year but remained incomplete as of April 2025.
findings.matters: Without effective risk management, organisations cannot identify emerging threats to financial or operational objectives. The audit committee's inability to fulfil its governance role indicates a fundamental oversight gap.
findings.figures: Gap existed for 'most of 2024/25'; risk arrangements still in development phase in April 2025
findings.quote: For most of 2024/25, adequate risk management arrangements were not in place for the Authority. As a result, the Audit and Governance Committee, which has overall responsibility for obtaining assurance on the effectiveness of the risk management framework and the management of strategic risks, has not been able to fulfil this role.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Head of Internal Audit YNYCA report 2025
findings.headline: Freedom of Information compliance at 74% of statutory deadline, significantly below Information Commissioner's Office expectation of 90-95%
findings.detail: The Authority achieved the 20-working-day statutory FoI deadline on 74% of requests in 2024/25. The Information Commissioner's Office expects 90-95% compliance. This performance gap was highlighted as a significant control weakness.
findings.matters: FoI compliance is a legal obligation. Performance at 74% against a 90-95% benchmark indicates process or capacity issues, suggesting the authority is struggling with administrative workflow management.
findings.figures: Authority performance: 74%; ICO expectation: 90-95%; statutory deadline: 20 working days
findings.quote: the ICO expects organisations to demonstrate that 90-95% of all Freedom of Information (FoI) requests are completed within the statutory time limit of 20 working days. The Authority's performance in 2024/25 was 74%.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Head of Internal Audit YNYCA report 2025
findings.headline: Multiple serious data security breaches in year, including incidents requiring reporting to Information Commissioner's Office
findings.detail: The Head of Internal Audit identified data security breaches as a significant control weakness. Several incidents were serious enough to require reporting to the ICO, indicating failures in data protection arrangements.
findings.matters: Data breaches indicate loss of control over sensitive information and trigger regulatory reporting obligations. Multiple incidents suggest systemic control issues rather than isolated lapses.
findings.figures: Exact number of breaches not specified; described as 'a number of serious' incidents requiring ICO reporting
findings.quote: there have been a number of serious data security beaches in the year, including incidents that have required reporting to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO).

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Head of Internal Audit YNYCA report 2025
findings.headline: Authority's control framework 'still relatively immature' with governance and risk management arrangements 'still in development'
findings.detail: As a newly established organisation, the control framework has not yet matured. Governance and risk management arrangements require further work to establish a comprehensive assurance framework. This reflects the early stage of the merged organisation's development.
findings.matters: An immature control framework in financial systems means weaknesses in how the council manages and accounts for money may go undetected. Peer councils and lenders need confidence that financial controls are robust.
findings.figures: Control framework described as 'relatively immature'; further work required on governance arrangements
findings.quote: As expected with any new organisation, the authority's control framework is still relatively immature. Governance and risk management arrangements are still in development with further work required to establish a comprehensive assurance framework.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Head of Internal Audit YNYCA report 2025
findings.headline: Head of Internal Audit issued 'limitation of scope' opinion, unable to form complete conclusion on adequacy of governance, risk management and control framework
findings.detail: The internal audit work did not provide sufficient evidence to fully assess whether the authority's control framework is working effectively. This occurred because the authority is newly established (2024/25 was its first full financial year) and its control framework remains immature. The audit covered only two financial systems across the entire authority.
findings.matters: A limitation of scope opinion means the audit committee and leadership lack full assurance that internal controls are operating effectively. For lenders and peer councils, this signals unresolved governance risks in a newly formed organisation.
findings.figures: First full financial year of combined authority; two financial systems audited
findings.quote: The results of the work carried out by Internal Audit, taken together with other sources of assurance, has led to a 'limitation of scope' opinion on the overall adequacy and effectiveness of the framework of governance, risk management and control operating at the York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority in 2024/25.
